newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Garuda plans freight price hikes by yr-end.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Garuda plans freight price hikes by yr-end.

text.p: Indonesia's national airline Garuda International said on Monday it planned price rises for its domestic and international freight operations by the end of the year due to the rising price of jet fuel.

Dede Suherman, tariff and pricing manager for Garuda's air freight operations, told Reuters the airline planned a price hike of between 15 and 25 percent for domestic cargo and between 5 and 10 percent for international cargo.
The exact increase depended on the routing of the flight, he said.
"The increasing price of jet kerosene is one factor in these (projected) price rises," Suherman said.
Asian jet kerosene rates have remained high despite a drop in world crude oil prices. Prices in the benchmark Singapore market were US $30.40 a barrel on Monday, up 30 percent year on year.
Airlines across the region are considering putting up both cargo and passenger fares as long as fuel prices show no sign of coming down.
Singapore Airline Ltd (SIA) said last month it would support moves to adjust fares at an emergency meeting of the 250-member International Air Transport Association (IATA) scheduled for November 13.
Pakistan's state-owned Pakistan International Airline (PIA) said last week it planned a 20 percent increase in passenger and cargo rates if fuel prices did not come down.
But Suherman said that he was not aware of any plan to further raise passenger airfares.
The government raised domestic airfares by as much as four percent in October, saying it was to counter a strengthening dollar.
Suherman said other domestic factors, such as inflation in the price of the Indonesian rupiah, also contributed to Garuda's decision to raise cargo tariffs.
"From 1993 until 1996 there has been no price rise (in cargo rates). But in those four years inflation has been around 10 percent a year," he said.
Indonesia's Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) has said it expects inflation to reach 8.5 percent this calendar year.
Suherman also pointed to increased costs in Garuda's domestic market operations after the airline launched its first cargo flight last week.
"We have to raise cargo tariffs to cover increased operating costs," he said.
The Boeing 737-200C, which serves domestic routes in eastern Indonesia from the country's second city Surabaya, is leased from Malaysia Airline Systems (MAS), a unit of Malaysia Airlines.
A second plane, which will begin flights soon, will serve western Indonesia and be based on Batam Island, 20 km (12 miles) south of Singapore.

Garuda has said it plans to expand its air cargo operations as it sees great potential for growth in the market. The government says it wants to develop Batam into an international cargo hub to rival Singapore's Changi airport.
